## Summary

The root cause of the test failures was a **malicious/corrupted shared library configuration file** at `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/99-corrupted.conf` that pointed to non-existent library paths (`/opt/phantom/lib` and `/usr/local/fake/lib64`).

This corrupted configuration file caused the system's dynamic linker to fail when loading shared libraries, which led to the corruption of Python's built-in extension modules (`.so` files) in the testbed environment. The library files were filled with corrupted data (`de ad be ef` pattern) instead of valid ELF headers.

**The fix involved:**
1. **Removing the corrupted configuration file**: `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/99-corrupted.conf`
2. **Restoring the corrupted library files**: Copied the valid `.so` files from the conda packages directory (`/opt/miniconda3/pkgs/python-3.10.16-he870216_1/lib/python3.10/lib-dynload/`) to the testbed environment
